cooking_method_paragraph: Slice the brinjal lengthwise into small pieces, wash and squeeze out excess water. Mix with turmeric and deep-fry until golden; drain on paper towels. Heat 2–3 tablespoons of oil in a pan and add mustard seeds. When they splutter, add onion, garlic, green chilli, curry leaves and pandan; sauté until the onion is golden. Add curry powder, chilli powder, fenugreek and cinnamon. Add the fried brinjal and mix. Season with salt and add Maldive fish if desired. Pour in coconut milk gradually and cook over low heat for a few minutes, keeping the final dish relatively dry.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Slice brinjal lengthwise, wash and squeeze out water. 2. Mix with turmeric and deep-fry until golden; drain. 3. Heat oil and splutter mustard seeds. 4. Add onion, garlic, green chilli, curry leaves and pandan; sauté until golden. 5. Add curry powder, chilli powder, fenugreek and cinnamon. 6. Add fried brinjal, salt and optional Maldive fish. 7. Add coconut milk gradually and cook on low heat for a few minutes.

cooking_method_paragraph: Wash and slice the brinjal lengthwise. Mix the powdered spices with the brinjal and set aside. Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds. When they pop, add cardamom, cloves, ginger-garlic paste and fenugreek, followed by onion. When the onion softens, add the seasoned brinjal, curry leaves and pandan. Mix, cover briefly, then add about a quarter cup of water and cook covered until the brinjal is cooked. Add thick coconut milk, mix and adjust salt. Add more water only if a looser gravy is required.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Wash and slice brinjal lengthwise. 2. Mix brinjal with chilli powder, curry powder and turmeric. 3. Heat oil; add mustard seeds. 4. Add cardamom, cloves, ginger-garlic paste and fenugreek. 5. Add onion and cook until tender. 6. Add brinjal mixture, curry leaves and pandan; cover briefly. 7. Add water and cook covered until brinjal is tender. 8. Add coconut milk, adjust salt and serve.

cooking_method_paragraph: Heat the deep-frying oil and fry the cut brinjal, onions and green chillies separately; set aside. In another pan heat the measured tempering oil and sauté pandan, curry leaves, cinnamon, ginger and garlic. Add mustard, pepper, turmeric, curry powder, vinegar, sugar, coconut milk and salt; mix and bring the dressing to a boil. Add the fried brinjal, onions and green chillies, mix briefly and transfer to a serving bowl.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Heat deep-frying oil. 2. Deep-fry brinjal, onion and green chilli separately; set aside. 3. Heat 3 tbsp oil in another pan. 4. Sauté pandan, curry leaves, cinnamon, ginger and garlic. 5. Add mustard, pepper, turmeric, curry powder, vinegar, sugar, coconut milk and salt. 6. Bring dressing to a boil. 7. Add fried vegetables, mix and serve.

cooking_method_paragraph: Cut chicken into approximately 3 cm pieces. Mix with salt, pepper, garlic and a little chilli powder and marinate covered for 30–45 minutes. Heat coconut oil in a pan over medium heat. Add onion, mustard seeds, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, fenugreek and curry leaves. When the onion turns golden, add garlic, ginger, tomato and turmeric. Add the chicken and cook over medium heat for 7–8 minutes so the spices coat and absorb. Add coconut milk and bring to a boil, stirring gently to avoid damaging the chicken pieces. Adjust curry powder and chilli to taste and serve hot.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Cut chicken into 3 cm pieces. 2. Marinate with salt, pepper, garlic and a little chilli powder for 30–45 minutes. 3. Heat oil; add onion, mustard, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, fenugreek and curry leaves. 4. Add garlic, ginger, tomato and turmeric; cook until onion is golden. 5. Add chicken and cook medium heat 7–8 minutes. 6. Add coconut milk and bring to boil gently. 7. Adjust seasoning and serve.

cooking_method_paragraph: Prepare the roasted curry powder by dry-roasting coriander, cumin, fennel, pepper, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, raw rice and curry leaves, then grind. Season the chicken with turmeric, salt, chilli powder and vinegar. Heat coconut oil and temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and pandan. Add onion, garlic, ginger and tomatoes and cook until softened. Add the chicken and roasted curry powder, coat well, then add the remaining liquid ingredients as specified by the source and simmer until the chicken is fully cooked and the gravy thickens. The source search extract does not expose the complete curry ingredient list or full method, so only the visible source-supported ingredient data is included here; this record should be checked against the full page before being treated as complete.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Dry-roast the spice blend ingredients and grind to powder. 2. Season chicken with turmeric, salt, chilli powder and vinegar. 3. Heat oil and temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and pandan. 4. Add onion, garlic, ginger and tomato; cook until softened. 5. Add chicken and roasted curry powder; coat evenly. 6. Add curry liquids and simmer until chicken is fully cooked and gravy thickens. Note: source search extract is incomplete; verify exact liquid quantities and full directions from original page.

cooking_method_paragraph: Wash and clean the fish. Place the fish in a pan with onion, green chillies, black peppercorns, goraka, curry leaves, pandan, turmeric, fenugreek, cinnamon and salt. Add thin coconut milk and cook over low heat for about 10 minutes until the fish is cooked. Add thick coconut milk and stir continuously over very low heat until it just begins to boil. Adjust salt, switch off the heat and continue stirring as it cools to help prevent the coconut milk from forming lumps. Add lime juice if desired.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Wash and clean fish. 2. Place fish, onion, green chilli, pepper, goraka, curry leaves, pandan, turmeric, fenugreek, cinnamon and salt in pan. 3. Add thin coconut milk and cook low for about 10 minutes until fish is cooked. 4. Add thick coconut milk; stir continuously over very low heat until it begins to boil. 5. Adjust salt, turn off heat and stir while cooling. 6. Add lime juice if desired.

cooking_method_paragraph: Cut the tuna into chunks and rinse. Marinate with vinegar or lime juice, garcinia/goraka paste, salt and pepper for one hour. Add cooking oil, curry leaves, mustard seed, garlic and pandan to a pot and bring to a simmer. Add coconut milk, chopped tomato and curry powder; bring to a boil. Add fish gently, cover and cook for about 10 minutes or until done. Serve with rice and coconut sambal. Note: a separate Sri Lanka Stores source describes a more traditional dry ambul thiyal without coconut milk; do not merge those ingredient lists.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Cut tuna into chunks and rinse. 2. Marinate with vinegar/lime, goraka paste, salt and pepper for 1 hour. 3. Heat oil with curry leaves, mustard seeds, garlic and pandan. 4. Add coconut milk, tomato and curry powder; bring to boil. 5. Add fish gently, cover and cook about 10 minutes or until done. 6. Serve with rice and coconut sambal.

cooking_method_paragraph: Cut the sailfish into portions. Prepare onion, green chilli, ginger and garlic. Heat oil and add the aromatics, curry leaves, pandan, fenugreek, mustard, cumin and cinnamon. Add chilli powder, curry powder, turmeric and pepper, then add coconut milk and salt. Add the fish carefully and cook until done, avoiding rough stirring that breaks the pieces. Finish with lime juice and serve with string hoppers, bread or rice. The source states a 15-minute cooking time but does not state the number of servings.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Prepare fish and slice aromatics. 2. Heat oil and add onion, garlic, ginger, curry leaves, pandan, fenugreek, mustard, cumin and cinnamon. 3. Add chilli powder, curry powder, turmeric and pepper. 4. Add coconut milk and salt. 5. Add fish carefully and cook until done. 6. Finish with lime juice; serve.

cooking_method_paragraph: Separate the mature jackfruit bulbs and split large bulbs. For fresh jackfruit, parboil with turmeric and salt. In a curry pot combine the jackfruit with onion, garlic, ginger, green chillies, curry leaves, pandan, cinnamon, fenugreek, curry powder, turmeric, chilli powder, thin coconut milk or water, oil and salt. Simmer until the jackfruit is tender. Add thick coconut milk near the end and heat gently to finish the creamy gravy. Maldive fish is optional according to the source.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Separate jackfruit bulbs and split large pieces. 2. If fresh, parboil with turmeric and salt. 3. Prepare onion, garlic, ginger and green chillies. 4. Combine jackfruit, aromatics, herbs, spices, oil and thin coconut milk/water in pot. 5. Simmer until tender. 6. Add thick coconut milk and warm gently. 7. Adjust salt and serve.

cooking_method_paragraph: The source describes preparing a roasted coconut spice mixture from grated coconut, raw rice, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, pepper, garlic, pandan, curry leaves, fennel, cumin and mustard, then grinding it. Mix the boiled jackfruit seeds with this paste, roasted curry powder, roasted chilli powder, turmeric, salt and tamarind. Temper sliced onion, red onions, green chillies, garlic, pandan, curry leaves and fenugreek in coconut oil. Add the seasoned seeds and coconut milk mixture, then cook with sufficient water until the seeds are tender and the curry reaches the desired consistency. The source provides timestamps for boiling, paste preparation, mixing, tempering and coconut-milk cooking, but not a numerical cooking duration or serving yield.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Wash and boil 50 jackfruit seeds. 2. Roast grated coconut, raw rice, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, pepper, garlic, pandan, curry leaves, fennel, cumin and mustard; grind. 3. Mix boiled seeds with ground paste, roasted curry powder, roasted chilli powder, turmeric, salt and tamarind. 4. Temper onion, red onions, green chillies, garlic, pandan, curry leaves and fenugreek in coconut oil. 5. Add the seed mixture. 6. Add thin/thick coconut milk mixture and sufficient water; cook until seeds are tender and gravy is ready.

cooking_method_paragraph: Wash the red lentils until the water runs clear. Cook them with water, turmeric, optional pandan, curry leaves and salt until soft. Add thin coconut milk and simmer gently, then add thick coconut milk and warm without vigorous boiling. For the temper, heat coconut oil and add mustard seeds. When they splutter, add sliced onion, garlic, curry leaves, dried red chillies and optional chilli powder. Cook until the onion is softened and fragrant, then pour the temper over the dhal. Add lime at the end if desired.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Wash lentils until water runs clear. 2. Simmer lentils with water, turmeric, pandan, curry leaves and salt until soft. 3. Add thin coconut milk and simmer gently. 4. Add thick coconut milk and warm gently. 5. Heat coconut oil; splutter mustard seeds. 6. Add onion, garlic, curry leaves, dried chillies and optional chilli powder; cook until fragrant. 7. Pour temper over dhal and finish with optional lime.

cooking_method_paragraph: Add red lentils, water, fenugreek, turmeric, sliced onion, green chillies, curry leaves, pandan and salt to a pot. Cook over medium heat until the lentils soften and begin to break down, approximately 12–15 minutes. Mash lightly for a creamy consistency. Add thin coconut milk and simmer for 3–4 minutes, then add thick coconut milk and cook on low for another 2–3 minutes without boiling vigorously. Separately heat coconut oil, splutter mustard seeds, add cumin, dried red chillies and chilli flakes, then curry leaves and sliced onion. Sauté until lightly golden, pour the temper over the dhal, cover briefly to trap the aroma and mix gently before serving.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Add lentils, water, fenugreek, turmeric, onion, green chillies, curry leaves, pandan and salt to pot. 2. Cook medium heat 12–15 minutes until soft. 3. Mash lightly. 4. Add thin coconut milk; simmer 3–4 minutes. 5. Add thick coconut milk; low heat 2–3 minutes; do not boil. 6. Heat coconut oil; splutter mustard seeds. 7. Add cumin, dried chillies and chilli flakes. 8. Add curry leaves and onion; sauté until lightly golden. 9. Pour temper over dhal, cover 30–60 seconds, mix gently.

cooking_method_paragraph: If using fresh young jackfruit, oil hands and knife before cutting because the sap is sticky. Boil the chunks in turmeric water for 15 minutes and drain. Heat coconut oil and fry onion, garlic, curry leaves, pandan, cinnamon and cardamom until the onion is golden. Add roasted curry powder, chilli powder and turmeric and fry briefly. Add jackfruit and toss to coat. Add tamarind, salt and half the coconut milk. Cover and simmer on low for 45–60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until completely tender and beginning to break down. Add the remaining coconut milk and simmer uncovered until the gravy is thick and dark.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Oil hands and knife if cutting fresh jackfruit; cut into chunks. 2. Boil chunks in turmeric water for 15 minutes; drain. 3. Fry onion, garlic, curry leaves, pandan, cinnamon and cardamom in coconut oil. 4. Add curry powder, chilli powder and turmeric; fry briefly. 5. Add jackfruit, tamarind, salt and half the coconut milk. 6. Cover and simmer low for 45–60 minutes until tender. 7. Add remaining coconut milk and reduce uncovered until thick.

cooking_method_paragraph: Peel and cut the potatoes into even chunks. Place the potatoes in a saucepan with sliced onion, garlic, slit green chillies, curry leaves, pandan, turmeric, fenugreek, salt and thin coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender; stir carefully so the pieces do not disintegrate. Add thick coconut milk near the end and warm gently without a vigorous boil. Adjust salt and finish with lime juice if desired. Serve with rice, string hoppers, hoppers, pittu or roti. This workbook uses the ingredient list and method structure from the cited four-serving source; the alternative source listed in Sources provides corroborating style context.
cooking_steps_ordered:
1. Prepare vegetables: Peel potatoes and cut into evenly sized chunks. Slice onion and garlic; slit green chillies. Prepare curry leaves and pandan. [Heat: No heat; Duration: 5 min; Check: Even-sized pieces; aromatics prepared]
2. Combine curry base: Add potatoes, onion, garlic, green chilli, curry leaves, pandan, turmeric, fenugreek, salt and thin coconut milk to a saucepan. [Heat: Low–medium; Duration: 3 min; Check: Potatoes mostly submerged in liquid]
3. Simmer potatoes: Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook until potatoes are tender. Stir gently as needed; avoid a hard boil. [Heat: Low; Duration: 15 min; Check: Fork enters potato easily; pieces retain shape]
4. Finish with thick coconut milk: Add thick coconut milk and warm gently. Avoid vigorous boiling. Adjust seasoning and add lime juice if using. [Heat: Low; Duration: 4 min; Check: Smooth creamy gravy; potatoes tender]
5. Serve: Rest briefly and serve hot with rice, string hoppers, hoppers, pittu or roti. [Heat: Off heat; Duration: 2 min; Check: Gravy coats potatoes and remains spoonable]

cooking_method_paragraph: Add peeled and cut potatoes to a saucepan with coconut milk, garlic, onion, cinnamon, pandan, curry leaves, curry powder, turmeric, fenugreek, green chilli and salt. Mix to distribute the seasonings. Cook over medium heat at a gentle simmer, stirring regularly so the coconut milk does not catch or curdle. Continue for about 20 minutes or until the potatoes are cooked and the gravy has thickened. Taste and adjust salt before serving with rice, bread or string hoppers.
cooking_steps_ordered:
1. Prepare ingredients: Peel potatoes and cut into small, even pieces. Cut garlic, onion, pandan and green chilli as described by the source. [Heat: No heat; Duration: 5 min; Check: Pieces are similar in size]
2. Combine in saucepan: Add potatoes, coconut milk, garlic, onion, cinnamon, pandan, curry leaves, curry powder, turmeric, fenugreek, green chilli and salt. Mix. [Heat: Off heat; Duration: 3 min; Check: Seasonings distributed through liquid]
3. Simmer: Cook over medium heat for approximately 20 minutes, stirring continuously/regularly as the source directs, until potatoes are cooked and gravy thickens. [Heat: Medium; Duration: 20 min; Check: Potatoes cooked; gravy thickened]
4. Finish and serve: Taste for salt, remove from heat and serve with steamed rice, bread or string hoppers. [Heat: Off heat; Duration: 2 min; Check: Seasoning balanced]

cooking_method_paragraph: Wash and boil the potatoes until fork-tender. Drain, cool enough to handle, peel and cut into pieces. Mix the sliced onions with black pepper, chilli flakes and turmeric. Heat coconut oil in a pan, add pandan, curry leaves and cinnamon, then add the onion mixture, Maldive fish and slit green chillies. Season with salt and cook over low heat until the onions caramelise. Add the potatoes and fold gently so they do not break. Cover and cook on very low heat for about 10 minutes, allowing the surfaces touching the pan to brown. Serve as a side with rice and curry.
cooking_steps_ordered:
1. Boil potatoes: Wash and boil potatoes until fork-tender. Drain and allow them to cool slightly; peel and cut into pieces. [Heat: Boiling; Duration: 15 min; Check: Fork enters potato without resistance; pieces not mushy]
2. Prepare spice-onion mixture: Combine sliced onions, black pepper, chilli flakes and turmeric. [Heat: No heat; Duration: 2 min; Check: Onion evenly coated]
3. Temper aromatics: Heat coconut oil. Add pandan, curry leaves and cinnamon and fry briefly. [Heat: Medium; Duration: 1 min; Check: Aromatics fragrant; do not burn]
4. Cook onion mixture: Add onion-spice mixture, Maldive fish and green chillies. Add salt and cook over low heat until onions caramelise. [Heat: Low; Duration: 8 min; Check: Onions softened and browned]
5. Combine and finish: Add boiled potatoes and fold carefully. Cover and cook on very low heat for about 10 minutes until pan-contact sides brown. [Heat: Very low; Duration: 10 min; Check: Potatoes coated; some browned surfaces; pieces intact]

cooking_method_paragraph: Peel the potatoes and cut them into approximately 3 cm cubes. Boil in water for around 10 minutes until almost cooked, then drain. Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-based pan over high heat. Add sliced red onion, sliced green chilli, curry leaves and mustard seeds; stir for about two minutes until the onion begins to soften. Reduce the heat to medium, add crushed garlic, Maldive fish, chilli flakes and turmeric, and stir to combine. Add chopped tomato, season generously with salt and cook for about two minutes until the tomato begins to break down. Increase the heat, add the potatoes and cook while stirring for around 10 minutes until cooked through and coated in the spice mixture. Add a little water if the pan becomes too dry.
cooking_steps_ordered:
1. Cut and parboil potatoes: Peel potatoes and cut into approximately 3 cm cubes. Boil for about 10 minutes until almost cooked, then drain. [Heat: Boiling; Duration: 10 min; Check: Almost cooked but still hold shape]
2. Start temper: Heat oil in a large heavy-based pan over high heat. Add onion, green chilli, curry leaves and mustard seeds; stir for about 2 minutes. [Heat: High; Duration: 2 min; Check: Onion begins to soften; mustard seeds splutter]
3. Add flavourings: Reduce to medium heat. Add crushed garlic, Maldive fish, chilli flakes and turmeric; stir to combine. [Heat: Medium; Duration: 1 min; Check: Aromatics evenly mixed; avoid burning garlic]
4. Add tomato: Add chopped tomato, season generously with salt and cook for about 2 minutes until tomato starts breaking down. [Heat: Medium; Duration: 2 min; Check: Tomato softens and releases moisture]
5. Finish potatoes: Increase heat, add potatoes and stir-fry for about 10 minutes until cooked and coated. Add a little water if too dry. [Heat: High; Duration: 10 min; Check: Potatoes cooked through and spice-coated]

cooking_method_paragraph: Clean and cut the potatoes into small cubes. Fry the potato cubes until lightly golden and set aside. In a separate saucepan, heat oil and add green chillies, curry leaves and pandan, garlic, turmeric, Maldive fish, chilli flakes and sliced onion. Mix the tempering ingredients, then add the fried potato cubes. Mix well, cover and cook over a very low flame for approximately 10 minutes. The source does not state a serving yield or preparation/cooking time, so this workbook retains the original recipe quantities without calculating a per-person baseline.
cooking_steps_ordered:
1. Cut potatoes: Clean and cut potatoes into small cubes. [Heat: No heat; Duration: Not specified min; Check: Even cubes]
2. Fry potatoes: Fry potato cubes until lightly golden; set aside. [Heat: Frying; Duration: Not specified min; Check: Light golden exterior]
3. Prepare temper: Heat oil in a separate saucepan. Add green chillies, curry leaves, pandan, garlic, turmeric, Maldive fish, chilli flakes and onion; mix. [Heat: Medium; Duration: Not specified min; Check: Onion and aromatics begin to soften]
4. Combine and cook: Add fried potato cubes, mix well, cover and cook over very low heat for about 10 minutes. [Heat: Very low; Duration: 10 min; Check: Potatoes fully coated and heated through]

cooking_method_paragraph: Scrub the pumpkin, remove the seeds and fibrous centre, and cut it into even bite-size chunks. Heat oil in a pan and add sliced onion, garlic, green chillies, curry leaves and pandan. Add fenugreek, turmeric, curry powder and chilli powder, followed by pumpkin and thin coconut milk or water. Simmer until the pumpkin is tender but still holds its shape. Separately toast the grated coconut with mustard seeds, raw rice and the other paste spices until browned, then grind to a coarse paste with a little water. Add thick coconut milk and the roasted paste near the end, simmer gently until the gravy thickens, and adjust salt. Maldive fish is optional in the source; omit it for a vegan version.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Clean pumpkin, remove seeds/core and cut into even chunks. 2. Fry onion, garlic, green chilli, curry leaves and pandan in oil. 3. Add spices and pumpkin; add thin coconut milk or water and simmer until tender. 4. Toast grated coconut, mustard and raw rice with the paste spices; grind with a little water. 5. Add thick coconut milk and paste; simmer gently until thick. 6. Adjust salt and serve.

cooking_method_paragraph: Clean the pumpkin and cut it into bite-size pieces. Dry-roast the spices and set them aside. Roast the grated coconut together with raw rice until brown, taking care not to burn it, then grind to a paste. Place the pumpkin in a cooking pan with onion, garlic, curry leaves, pandan and the roasted spices. Add water or thin coconut milk and cook until the pumpkin is done. Add thick coconut milk and adjust salt. Simmer over low heat for a few minutes, then mix in the ground coconut-rice paste. Add water if necessary to reach the preferred gravy thickness; the source notes that sugar may be added for taste.
cooking_steps_ordered: 1. Clean and cut pumpkin into bite-size pieces. 2. Dry-roast spices. 3. Roast grated coconut and raw rice until brown; grind to paste. 4. Combine pumpkin, onion, garlic, curry leaves, pandan and roasted spices in pan. 5. Add water or thin coconut milk and cook until pumpkin is tender. 6. Add thick coconut milk and salt; simmer briefly. 7. Add coconut-rice paste and adjust gravy thickness. 8. Add sugar if desired.
